source_caption:
One of the greatest scenes in Spider-Man history. 🕷️

There’s something almost biblical about the way Raimi stages this scene. Peter’s arms are stretched out, he’s wounded and unconscious, and the people around him pass his body from one person to another like they’re carrying someone who has sacrificed himself for them.

But when they finally see Peter’s face, they don’t see Spider-Man anymore. They see a young, exhausted and vulnerable kid.

Peter’s first instinct is fear. He’s terrified that his identity has been exposed. Instead, the people protect him. They keep his secret and help him without asking for anything in return.

And that’s what makes this scene so powerful. It shows that being a hero isn’t only about the person behind the mask. Sometimes, it’s about the people who choose to stand beside them.

For Peter, this is the moment he truly understands what being Spider-Man means. The responsibility may be his, but he doesn’t have to carry it alone.
